statement.p: Find the area lying outside r=6\cos\theta and inside r=3 + 3 \cos\theta.

static.solution:
r=6\cos\theta is a circle with radius 3 centered on (3,0), while r=3 + 3 \cos\theta is a cardioid that entirely encloses the circle. Therefore, to find the area, we subtract the area enclosed by the circle from that enclosed by the cardioid.
The cardioid, r=3 + 3 \cos\theta, is traced out as \theta goes from \theta=0 to \theta=2\pi. Thus, remembering that the area enclosed by a region lying within the polar equation r = f(\theta) is Area= \int_\alpha^\beta\,{1\over2}(f(\theta))^2\,d\theta, \hbox{Area of cardioid } = \int_0^{2\pi}{1\over2}(3 + 3 \cos\theta)^2\,d\theta. The circle is traced out as \theta goes from \theta=0 to \theta=\pi, so its area is \hbox{Area of circle }= \int_0^{\pi}{1\over2}(6\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta. Of course, because the circle has radius 3, we know this second integral will evaluate to 9 \pi.
We can find the area of the cardioid, \int_0^{2\pi}{1\over2}(3 + 3 \cos\theta)^2\,d\theta = {1\over2}\int_0^{2\pi} 9 (1 + 2\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta)\,d\theta, numerically by using a calculator, or by parts, or using a table of integrals, to find that the area of the cardioid is A = {27\pi\over 2}.
Thus, the area enclosed by the cardioid that lies outside of the circle is given by A = {27\pi\over 2} - 9\pi = {9\pi\over 2}.
